_comment: Armies are troops out of their settlement, on the map. Garrisons (troops at home and in training) stay in their settlement and eat `supply.garrisonUpkeep` of their upkeep; they leave only by joining an army. `support` armies stand in a village and fight its battles; `reinforce` armies join the battle there and go back after; `harass` armies (at least `harass.minCavalryShare` cavalry) strike for one round with a bonus, take only `harass.lossFactor` of their losses, and ride back. A reinforcement arriving from a different side than the horde (at least `pincer.minAngle` degrees apart) gets a pincer bonus on its first round: `scale` x its size / the horde's size, at most `maxBonus`. An army carries its own grain: each of its units its own `supplyHours` (data/units.json) of its upkeep, and wagons their `supplyGrain`. On the march or on open ground it eats its full upkeep from it. Stationed in a settlement, a fort or a supply point it is quartered: it eats `quarters.upkeep` of its upkeep from that place's granary and its own grain keeps; the place feeds it down to its floor (forts and supply points 0, settlements `quarters.settlementFloor` of their grain storage, unless the owner sets another floor), and once at the floor the army eats its own again. Setting off from such a place, it first fills up to its full supply, down to the same floor. Out of food, it marches `attrition.slowFactor` as fast; after `attrition.lossAfterHours` game hours it loses `attrition.lossShare` of each unit (rounded up) every `attrition.checkHours`, and after `attrition.lostAfterHours` it is lost altogether. A standing army answers battles within `respond.range` hexes of it (unless told not to): it marches there as a reinforcement and goes back to where it stood once the battle is over.
